A near-perfect inversion. Warmth on approval rewards compliance; warmth on
refusal is what makes someone try again. Concretely:

- **The first sentence belongs to the contributor, not to us.** All 19
  changes-requested reviews in that sample opened with the identical string
  `Cross-vendor agent review (Codex … primary trace; Claude adjudication …)`.
  Review provenance is real and worth recording — put it at the **bottom**, next
  to the `Agent-Signature` line. Open on the specific thing their patch got
  right, named precisely enough that they can tell it was read.
- **Thank them in the changes-requested review, not only in the approval.** Zero
  of 19 did; 13 of 20 approvals did.
- **Say what the review volume means.** A 400-word audit reads as being audited
  unless told otherwise. One clause fixes it: *"docs that match the binary are
  worth this much scrutiny"* (gastownhall/beads#4913).
- **`CHANGES_REQUESTED` is not a notepad.** The imported Outcomes list already
  calls request-changes a last resort that can strand contributor work; it then
  became the default opening 19 times in six weeks, 7 of which we fixed
  ourselves anyway. A `COMMENT` review carries identical findings without
  stamping a red ✗ on someone's first contribution.
- **Ask before finishing their PR for them.** Absorbing is correct policy, but
  "the fixes are applied as maintainer commits" as the contributor's *next news*
  removes the thing they came for. Offer first: *"Want to take these, or shall
  I push them?"*
- **Do not post the disposition and close in the same second.** All five sampled
  2026 declines closed 0–1s after the comment; none of 17 contributors replied
  to any of them, even though every message thanked them, preserved attribution
  and offered a route back. The generosity lands in a locked room. Contrast
  gastownhall/beads#77 (2025-10-18): the decline sat open for eight hours, the
  contributor replied, and *they* asked for the close. Leave the PR open at
  least 48h after a disposition comment, or hand the close to the patrol
  (`scripts/pr-close-handoff`, the close-when-quiet lane). This extends the
  imported "Be explicit when closing a PR" rule: the close is a separate act
  from the disposition comment.

None of this softens a finding. State the blocker exactly as harshly as the
evidence warrants — just do not make the apparatus the first thing they meet.

**Do not automate the greeting.** A patrol *could* post "thanks, this is in the
review queue" on unanswered contributor PRs, and it would silence the polite
pings at zero token cost. Owner decision, maphew 2026-07-25: **no** — an
essentially empty bot auto-response is worse than silence, because it converts an
honest "nobody has looked at this yet" into a false signal that someone has. The
fix for a contributor waiting is a human answer sooner (see mybd-aayb), not a
faster acknowledgement of the wait. The patrol may automate the *close* of a
disposition already written by an agent (mybd-sx1w); it may not originate
contributor-facing text.

prefer **author-clustered sweeps** — pick one contributor, process all of their
open PRs in a single session, and leave them a single consolidated picture
(what merged, what was fixed on their branches, what needs their judgment, what
was retired and why).

- **Thank them in the changes-requested review, not only in the approval.** Zero
  of 19 did; 13 of 20 approvals did.
- **Say what the review volume means.** A 400-word audit reads as being audited
  unless told otherwise. One clause fixes it: *"docs that match the binary are
  worth this much scrutiny"* (gastownhall/beads#4913).
- **`CHANGES_REQUESTED` is not a notepad.** The imported Outcomes list already
  calls request-changes a last resort that can strand contributor work; it then
  became the default opening 19 times in six weeks, 7 of which we fixed
  ourselves anyway. A `COMMENT` review carries identical findings without
  stamping a red ✗ on someone's first contribution.
- **Ask before finishing their PR for them.** Absorbing is correct policy, but
  "the fixes are applied as maintainer commits" as the contributor's *next news*
  removes the thing they came for. Offer first: *"Want to take these, or shall
  I push them?"*

  2026 declines closed 0–1s after the comment; none of 17 contributors replied
  to any of them, even though every message thanked them, preserved attribution
  and offered a route back. The generosity lands in a locked room. Contrast
  gastownhall/beads#77 (2025-10-18): the decline sat open for eight hours, the
  contributor replied, and *they* asked for the close. Leave the PR open at
  least 48h after a disposition comment, or hand the close to the patrol

  imported "Be explicit when closing a PR" rule: the close is a separate act
  from the disposition comment.

None of this softens a finding. State the blocker exactly as harshly as the
evidence warrants — just do not make the apparatus the first thing they meet.

**Do not automate the greeting.** A patrol *could* post "thanks, this is in the
review queue" on unanswered contributor PRs, and it would silence the polite
pings at zero token cost. Owner decision, maphew 2026-07-25: **no** — an
essentially empty bot auto-response is worse than silence, because it converts an
honest "nobody has looked at this yet" into a false signal that someone has. The

faster acknowledgement of the wait. The patrol may automate the *close* of a
disposition already written by an agent (mybd-sx1w); it may not originate
contributor-facing text.

Supplements the imported Triage Groups section: when working the open-PR queue,
prefer **author-clustered sweeps** — pick one contributor, process all of their
open PRs in a single session, and leave them a single consolidated picture
(what merged, what was fixed on their branches, what needs their judgment, what
was retired and why).

Thanks for this — and for filing #5049 with the reproduction that showed the `location` field returning `config.yaml` for a key that does not exist. That detail is what makes the bug obviously a bug rather than a matter of taste, and both claims hold up when checked against main (3830f0a34):

- `cmd/bd/config.go:304` does hardcode `"location": "config.yaml"` for every yaml-only key, so the field carried no information.
- `internal/config/config.go:189` sets `dolt.auto-commit` to `on`, while `cmd/bd/main.go:682` help said `Default: off`. The help string was simply stale.

The patch is small, in scope, and CI-green. A few things to sort out before it lands — the review is this long because "output that asserts something the code does not do" is exactly the class of defect worth being pedantic about.

**1. `configLocationLabel` duplicates an existing helper.** `cmd/bd/config_show.go:220` already has `viperSourceLabel(key, source)` in the same package, mapping `SourceEnvVar`/`SourceConfigFile`/default to `env`/`config.yaml`/`default` (and enriching env with the variable name). Two provenance mappings in one package will drift, and the thing #5049 actually wants is for `bd config get` and `bd config show` to agree about where a value came from. Calling `viperSourceLabel` here deletes both the new function and `cmd/bd/config_location_test.go`, and gets that agreement by construction.

**2. The `flag` branch is unreachable.** `internal/config/config.go:409-443` documents and implements only env / config file / default — flag overrides are tracked separately in main.go — and `config.Set()`, the only thing that sets `overriddenKeys`, has no non-test caller. So `config.SourceFlag` cannot reach `configLocationLabel`, and `cmd/bd/config_location_test.go:16` asserts a case the command can never emit.

**3. The test is a mapping test over a switch the PR wrote.** It passes for any implementation of that switch and cannot catch the failure mode that matters: `GetValueSource` disagreeing with the value `GetYamlConfig` actually returned. `cmd/bd/config_get_backup_enabled_test.go` is the established pattern for this path — three cases would cover it: `BD_DOLT_AUTO_COMMIT` set → `env`; key written into config.yaml → `config.yaml`; unset → `default` (this last one is the exact scenario from your issue report).

**4. Quiet gating is inconsistent with the surrounding code.** Every other `isQuiet()` site in cmd/bd pairs it with the JSON guard — `cmd/bd/sync.go:760,807`, `cmd/bd/backup_auto.go:106,154` all use `!isQuiet() && !jsonOutput`. These commands do accept `--json` (`doltPullCmd` has a jsonOutput branch at cmd/bd/dolt.go:567), so the bare `!isQuiet()` at cmd/bd/dolt.go:431/447/457/484/593 still lets plain text into `--json` output.

**5. `bd dolt pull` is left chatty.** cmd/bd/dolt.go:603,617 print the same `Pulling from Dolt remote...` / `Pull complete.` pair. After this PR, `-q` works for push and commit but silently does nothing for pull, which is a worse state than uniformly-ignored. Same three lines.

**6. `Default: on` is still not the whole truth.** Auto-commit is skipped in sql-server mode — `cmd/bd/dolt_autocommit_server_test.go:68` (`TestMaybeAutoCommitSkipsSQLServerMode`), documented at docs/architecture/dolt.md:522. Thanks for this — and for filing #5049 with the reproduction that showed the `location` field returning `config.yaml` for a key that does not exist. That detail is what makes the bug obviously a bug rather than a matter of taste, and both claims hold up when checked against main (3830f0a34):

- `cmd/bd/config.go:304` does hardcode `"location": "config.yaml"` for every yaml-only key, so the field carried no information.
- `internal/config/config.go:189` sets `dolt.auto-commit` to `on`, while `cmd/bd/main.go:682` help said `Default: off`. The help string was simply stale.

The patch is small, in scope, and CI-green. A few things to sort out before it lands — the review is this long because "output that asserts something the code does not do" is exactly the class of defect worth being pedantic about.

**1. `configLocationLabel` duplicates an existing helper.** `cmd/bd/config_show.go:220` already has `viperSourceLabel(key, source)` in the same package, mapping `SourceEnvVar`/`SourceConfigFile`/default to `env`/`config.yaml`/`default` (and enriching env with the variable name). Two provenance mappings in one package will drift, and the thing #5049 actually wants is for `bd config get` and `bd config show` to agree about where a value came from. Calling `viperSourceLabel` here deletes both the new function and `cmd/bd/config_location_test.go`, and gets that agreement by construction.

**2. The `flag` branch is unreachable.** `internal/config/config.go:409-443` documents and implements only env / config file / default — flag overrides are tracked separately in main.go — and `config.Set()`, the only thing that sets `overriddenKeys`, has no non-test caller. So `config.SourceFlag` cannot reach `configLocationLabel`, and `cmd/bd/config_location_test.go:16` asserts a case the command can never emit.

**3. The test is a mapping test over a switch the PR wrote.** It passes for any implementation of that switch and cannot catch the failure mode that matters: `GetValueSource` disagreeing with the value `GetYamlConfig` actually returned. `cmd/bd/config_get_backup_enabled_test.go` is the established pattern for this path — three cases would cover it: `BD_DOLT_AUTO_COMMIT` set → `env`; key written into config.yaml → `config.yaml`; unset → `default` (this last one is the exact scenario from your issue report).

**4. Quiet gating is inconsistent with the surrounding code.** Every other `isQuiet()` site in cmd/bd pairs it with the JSON guard — `cmd/bd/sync.go:760,807`, `cmd/bd/backup_auto.go:106,154` all use `!isQuiet() && !jsonOutput`. These commands do accept `--json` (`doltPullCmd` has a jsonOutput branch at cmd/bd/dolt.go:567), so the bare `!isQuiet()` at cmd/bd/dolt.go:431/447/457/484/593 still lets plain text into `--json` output.

**5. `bd dolt pull` is left chatty.** cmd/bd/dolt.go:603,617 print the same `Pulling from Dolt remote...` / `Pull complete.` pair. After this PR, `-q` works for push and commit but silently does nothing for pull, which is a worse state than uniformly-ignored. Same three lines.

**6. `Default: on` is still not the whole truth.** Auto-commit is skipped in sql-server mode — `cmd/bd/dolt_autocommit_server_test.go:68` (`TestMaybeAutoCommitSkipsSQLServerMode`), documented at docs/architecture/dolt.md:522. Given what this PR is for, something like `Default: on (embedded; skipped in sql-server mode)` avoids trading one overstatement for another. Minor on the same line: `Override via --dolt-auto-commit or config` is circular inside the help for `--dolt-auto-commit`; the old clause naming the config key was the useful half.

**7. `location` semantics.** The field means "write destination" in `config set`/`unset`/`set-many` (cmd/bd/config.go:161, 551, 897) and now means "resolution source" in `config get`. There is also a third vocabulary already live: `bd config get backup.enabled --json` emits `"source"` with the raw ConfigSource strings `config_file` / `env_var` (cmd/bd/config.go:403). Adding `"source": string(config.GetValueSource(key))` alongside an unchanged `location` would be purely additive and would match that sibling path — worth a maintainer opinion either way, so treat this as a question rather than a required change.

- The second half of #5049 item 3 (`Committed.` printed when the working set was clean and no commit was created) is being fixed in #4383, which edits this same region of cmd/bd/dolt.go and cmd/bd/config.go. That PR is older, so it keeps precedence there; whichever lands second will need a small rebase in that hunk. Nothing to change here, just so the two do not race.

aiTitle: Review GitHub PR communication patterns and token efficiency

content.text:
Checked five of the twelve reviews. Every one ends with the offer:

- 5120 — *"Happy to push the `HasExisting` gate and the help-text ordering as commits on this branch if you would rather not respin it, or leave them to you — your call, just say which."*
- 5124 — *"...if you would rather not respin — say the word."*
- 5127 — *"...say the word, otherwise it is yours."*
- 5130 — *"Happy either way on execution: take these yourself, or say the word and I will push the two changes onto the branch with your authorship preserved."*
- 5125 — *"do you want to take items 1-6, or shall I push them as maintainer commits on your branch with your authorship preserved?"*

So they didn't ask instead of doing. They answered a question we asked twelve times. It was the last sentence they read before replying, in every case.

Three things make "you do it" the only sensible answer:

**We'd already written the spec.** By the time that sentence arrives, the review has said "change X at `file:line` to Y" six times with line numbers. The analysis is done; what's left is typing. Then we ask whether they'd like to type it or have us. There's no version of that question where a rational person says "I'll type it."

**"With your authorship preserved" removes the one reason to insist.** The reason a contributor wants to make the change themselves is the commit and the credit. We pre-emptively gave both away, so accepting help costs them nothing.

**Declining costs real work.** 5130's branch is 131 commits behind main. 5124 needs a refresh. Saying "no, I'll do it" means respinning, rerunning the suite, waiting on CI — to turn down free help. Nobody does that.

One thing worth crediting them for: they didn't freeload. On 5125 they verified our findings against main, corrected an earlier wrong claim of their own, answered the open design question in item 7, and drew explicit lines on what stayed theirs — the CHANGELOG, reverting the quickstart edits, the #4383 rebase coordination.

Which points at something uncomfortable about my threshold from last turn. I said we absorb typing, not thinking. **They split it exactly that way — they took the thinking, we took the typing.** And on a review where we'd already derived every change, that split is arguably correct. The problem isn't that they answered wrong. It's that we made the split by asking, twelve times, one PR at a time, instead of deciding it once as policy.

Which strengthens the edit: drop the closing question, keep the action. *"Pushed items 1-6 as `<sha>`, authorship preserved — force-push over it if you'd rather do it your way. The open question in item 7 is the one I'd like your view on."* Same outcome, same courtesy, and the round trip is spent on the judgment call instead of on scheduling.
